sections.overview: Eupackardia calleta is the sole described species of its genus, a North and Central American silkmoth in Saturniidae.
sections.identification: Adults have black wings with conspicuous white lines and spots, a dark body with red markings, and an 8–11 cm wingspan.
sections.habitat: The species ranges from Central America north into Mexico and the southwestern United States, including Arizona and southern Texas.
sections.diet: Caterpillars use several woody hosts, including ceniza, ash and privet; a Texas field paper confirms natural feeding on Ligustrum.
sections.behavior: Young caterpillars feed in groups, whereas older larvae usually feed alone; adults emerge in the evening.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in clusters on host leaves; cocoons are attached to twigs, commonly near the ground and in shade.
sections.ecology: Its larvae can use different shrubs and trees in the olive family; the Texas study documents a natural host record beyond the main regional host.
sections.conservation: The consulted sources provide distribution and natural-history records but no current formal global conservation assessment.
